praveen: Oops — ran a new synthetic generator build against the 2.3 runtime to reproduce that tail regression. Want to dump the experiment notes here.

praveen: Goal: mix steady Poisson baseline (QPS 120), episodic gamma-shaped bursts (peak 2k qps for 2s), and KV-warmup sequences so kernel-selection + batching behavior matches production traces.

alisa: Nice. Is this the one that toggles KV cache hits by prefixing a small fanout before each burst? That helped us repro last time.

praveen: Exactly. Pattern is: for each episode -> send 10 short priming requests (len 8) with distinct keys -> pause 50ms -> burst of long requests (len 512) drawn from gamma envelope. That forces cold KV pressure and then heavy KV reuse mid-burst.

ben: Can you paste the config you used? I want to plug it into the harness and run on the 4xA100 cluster.

praveen: Sure, pasted chunk:
```
pattern: {
  baseline: {type: poisson, qps: 120}
  episodes: {
    rate_envelope: gamma(shape=2.5, scale=0.6)
    peak_qps: 2000
    duration_s: 2
    kv_priming: {n:10, keyset: session_YYYY, pause_ms:50}
    long_req_len: 512
  }
  seed: 20260314
}
```

marta: Nice and compact. When you ran it, what did the kernel-selection logs show? Any unexpected fallback to the float kernel?

praveen: That's the thing — at the start of each burst we saw frequent kernel flips: fast int8 path fails first 30 tokens for some sequences, falls back to float kernels, then flips back after KV is warmed. Profiling snippet:
```
[2026-03-14T14:02:12Z] kernel_select: model_x -> int8 (ok)
[2026-03-14T14:02:12Z] kernel_exec: int8 failed (nan-check) -> fallback float
[2026-03-14T14:02:12Z] kernel_select: model_x -> float
[2026-03-14T14:02:12Z] 1.2s later -> int8 re-enable
```

chad: That flip cost would explain the tail spikes. The runtime currently invalidates microkernels on NaN, but we should prefer a soft-degrade that pins kernel but marks sequences to skip quant path rather than global invalidation.

alisa: Also check batching heuristics. If priming makes many small sequences start at near-same time, continuous batching might form awkwardly: small batch for first 30 tokens -> then sudden big batch when long requests come in -> kernel mismatch.

ben: On the 4xA100 run I saw increased variance: p50 unchanged, p95 +30ms, p99 +180ms during bursts. Here's a short table I copied from dashboard:
```
baseline: p50 6ms p95 28ms p99 95ms
during-burst: p50 8ms p95 58ms p99 275ms
```

marta: Those numbers look similar to what we saw in the prod regression. Did you enable KV prefix caching? That can change the early token behavior.

praveen: For this experiment KV prefix caching is default-off so priming actually touches cold entries. Wanted to stress miss/hit transition. I also toggled an alternate batching policy (max_wait_ms=8 vs default 4). It reduced p99 by ~20ms but increased p50 by ~1ms.

chad: Worth trying a hybrid: aggressive batching for steady-state but a burst-detect window that reduces wait to 1ms when envelope slope > threshold. That avoids creating large batches with mixed kernels.

alisa: Also instrument per-request kernel metadata in trace: add fields kernel_hint/selected_kernel and batch_id -> then we can do apples-to-apples comparison between runs and see if p99 aligns with kernel flips or KV misses.

praveen: Did that. Raw trace sample for a single high-tail request:
```
req_id: abc123
start: 14:02:12.104
priming: 10 reqs -> keys (kv) -> miss
selected_kernel: int8 -> fallback float @ token 34
batch_id: 78
kv_cache_state: miss->partial_hit
end: 14:02:12.379
latency: 275ms
```

ben: If fallback happens at token 34, the system already spent time on int8 kernels. Might be cheaper to pre-validate first token's numeric stability and choose kernel proactively for the whole sequence.

marta: Agreed. Pre-flight check: run a small stateless numeric-sanity on the input embeddings (cheap) and bias toward float only if bad. Also consider doing an early KV probe to decide batch placement.

chad: Implementation plan suggestion:
- Add preflight numeric check (2-3 tokens) to kernel selector
- Introduce burst-mode batching window when envelope derivative > x
- Keep KV priming tool in generator and add a flag to flip to prefix-caching mode
- Run apples-to-apples: same seed + same cluster + toggle single knob each run

praveen: I'll codify flags and push a harness run tomorrow. ci-bot: scheduling a 3h job on perf-cluster-4xA100 starting 2026-03-15T09:00Z

ci-bot: Job scheduled: perf-1768802042-run1 -> ressources reserved

ben: When you have results, drop p50/p95/p99 + kernel-fallback counts + KV miss ratio. If fallback_count correlates with p99, we can prioritize kernel-selector changes.

alisa: And include burst-episode histograms (latency vs time-since-episode-start) so we can see warmup slope.

praveen: Will do. Also adding a short README in the harness dir describing the seedcraft pattern and knobs.

marta: Awesome. Thanks for capturing this thread. TL;DR: generator reproduces a kernel-fallback induced tail via KV cold->warm transitions; try preflight numeric check + burst-aware batching to reduce p99.

praveen: Yep. Tagging @chad for kernel fallback follow-up and @alisa for batching heuristics. Will post results here.
